# URLCode store

> Operator-installed declarative data store extension for URLCode. Declare
> typed collections in `urlcode.yaml`, mount each with `extension: store`, and
> the extension serves a bounded JSON CRUD API backed by one operator-owned
> SQLite database (`node:sqlite`, Node only). No handler code. Installed with
> `urlcode extensions add store`; not an independent security assessment. Apache-2.0.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.store: { version: "1", config: { collections: { <name>: { fields, sortable, filterable, readOnly, ... } } } }`
- A mount per collection, e.g. `/api/notes/*: { extension: store, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE] }`
- Protect the mount with `auth: true` (the example adds it when auth is installed) unless the
  example's explicit `--ack store:public-write` was given; an unprotected write mount has no rate
  limiting, abuse protection or multi-tenant isolation of its own.
- The store serves JSON only; the frontend is the application's own (`fetch` to the mounts, reading
  `etags` and `may` from a list), as `proofs/private-requests/client` does.
- `urlcode extensions add store` writes an empty `collections` block and no mount; `--example`
  adds the `todos` collection on `/api/todos` (API only); with
  auth installed the mount gets `auth: true` and the collection `ownership: owner` (per-user
  records) and, with audit installed, `audit: true`.
- `audit: true` on a collection records every write in the audit extension's log (field names, never
  values) through an outbox table written in the same transaction; at 1000 undelivered events writes answer `503 audit_backlog`.
  Activation refuses it without the audit extension or on a mount no principal-providing policy guards
  (for example `auth: true`). Short-link clicks are never audited.
- `ownership: owner` on a collection scopes every request to the principal a policy such as
  `auth: true` on its mount sets; without it (the default) a collection is shared. An owned
  collection may add `maxRecordsPerOwner: N` (at most `maxRecords`): a principal holding N records
  gets `409 owner_quota_exceeded`; `maxRecords` still caps the whole collection.
- Conditional state changes: `transitions.<name>: {from, set, stamp?, by?, mount?}` on a collection
  serves `POST <mount>/<id>/<name>` (one record, exact `from` values, constant `set` values, `actor`/`now`
  stamps, `If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key`; `409 transition_conflict` otherwise). `by: others` on an owned
  collection lets any principal but the owner act, on its own guarded mount; properties declared `readOnly: true`
  change only through a transition. `idempotency: {maxKeys}` replays a retried key (same request: first
  status, current record; different request: `422 idempotency_key_reused`). Interval constraints and
  multi-record transfers are not declarative: a host extension uses `StoreExports.transaction(work)`.
- Stored short links: `extensions.store.config.shortLinks.<name>: {mount, collection, destination, clicks}`
  over a collection with a `key`, a required `format: uri` destination property (HTTP(S) only) and one
  `increments` counter, plus a route `<mount>/*: {extension: store, methods: [GET, HEAD]}`; no
  function. See the README's "Short links" example.
- `urlcode-store reassign --database <file> --project <app> --from <id>
  --to <id> [--collection <name>] [--dry-run] [--actor <id>]` moves one principal's records to another in one
  transaction (it may run while the server serves); it refuses as a whole if `--to` would exceed a collection's
  `maxRecordsPerOwner` or an audited collection's outbox backlog, records each moved record
  (`store.record.reassigned`) on an `audit: true` collection, and moves `--from`'s membership in every
  `membership: true` collection with the records. `--actor` (default `operator`) is operator-asserted, not
  authenticated; `ownerless-assign`/`ownerless-delete` take `--project` and `--actor` and record the same way.
- `urlcode-store members add|remove|list --database <file> --project <app> --collection <name> [--principal <id>]`
  maintains a membership collection (no HTTP API exists for it). `audit: true` on it records every added and removed
  member in the same transaction. `readers.showOwner: true` shows the owner's principal id as `_owner` on the readers
  mount only.
- The operator activates it in the site's `host.mjs` with `store()` (or `store({database})`) in
  the `composeHost` list; `urlcode extensions add store` writes that line.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): install, scaffold, host options, short links, and a generated field reference
  for every configuration key at the end.
- [docs/STORE.md](../../docs/STORE.md): the full HTTP contract, limits and concurrency guarantees.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): trust boundary, the database file, `ETag`/`If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key` scoping.

## Do not guess
- No CRUD or persistence code in project `function`/`middleware` routes; declare the
  collection. Those routes run trusted and in-process, but hold no store authority of their own.
- One server process per database (supported, not enforced); each request is one SQLite
  transaction over one record; last write wins unless a caller sends `If-Match`; a repeated
  `Idempotency-Key` replays the first answer's status with the record as it is now, and the same key on a
  different request is `422`.
- `sortable`/`filterable` field lists are declared per collection; `?sort=`/`?<field>=` queries
  against an undeclared name, or a filter value the field can never hold (outside its `enum`, `minimum`/`maximum`,
  `minLength`/`maxLength` or `format`), are `400`s, not silently ignored.
- The database is operator-owned, outside the project, on local disk, not a network
  filesystem; the store creates its directory `0700` and the file `0600`.
- The `store-schema` artifact is the configuration schema and an example as inert JSON:
  adding it does not register `store` or grant data access.
